frontmatter.title: `documentvisitor` — base visitor for traversal:

blocks.content: The `DocumentVisitor` class serves as the foundational base for traversing and processing Aspose.Note document structures in Python. It enables developers to implement custom logic for inspecting or modifying nodes during a depth-first walk through the document tree—ideal for tasks like exporting, validation, or transformation.

Built-in iteration support via `GetEnumerator()` allows intuitive node traversal using standard Python syntax such as `for child in node:`, making document navigation more natural and expressive in note python code. This pattern aligns with common Python idioms used in note taking app development and professional note workflows.

items: The `Document` property enables upward traversal to the root `Document`, allowing access to the top-level node from any descendant in the tree
The `Page(CompositeNode)` class supports hierarchical document structures by inheriting from `CompositeNode`, enabling page-level content composition
The `Title(CompositeNode)` class provides structured title handling for pages, also inheriting from `CompositeNode` for nested content management

blocks.content: The `DocumentVisitor` pattern in Aspose.Note enables traversal of document nodes for custom processing. Using the `CompositeNode(Node)` base class, developers can implement visitors that walk through `Page`, `Outline`, `OutlineElement`, and `RichText` nodes. This approach supports parsing, transformation, or extraction of content such as page titles and inline text. The `Title` property on `Page` and its `TitleText` sub-property provide access to structured title content, while `RichText.Text` exposes the underlying string value for further processing.

The `DocumentVisitor` pattern enables structured traversal of OneNote document hierarchies. For practical use, explore how to access page metadata and content elements using the properties and iteration methods defined in the API surface.
